title: Smoked Salmon Kedgeree
subtitle: Anglo-Indian kedgeree with smoked salmon instead of haddock
excerpt: Basmati rice with smoked salmon, hard-boiled eggs, spring onions, and a hint of curry spice. A lighter, quicker spin on the classic British breakfast kedgeree.

recipe.sourceNotes: This is a variation on the traditional kedgeree (see the main kedgeree recipe) that replaces smoked haddock with cold-smoked salmon. The result is lighter and faster to make, since cold-smoked salmon does not need poaching: it is simply stirred through the finished rice and allowed to warm through from the residual heat. Smoked salmon kedgeree is popular as a lighter brunch or lunch dish and has the advantage of being made with ingredients that can be kept in the fridge without the need to poach fish to order. The spicing is identical to the original kedgeree.

content.text: Remove the smoked salmon from the fridge 20 minutes before using: cold salmon added to warm rice will cool the dish too quickly. Tear it into strips rather than dicing it: this maintains a more interesting texture. Add it off the heat and fold through gently, allowing the residual heat to warm it through without cooking it.

Cook the rice in salted water according to packet instructions. Drain, rinse briefly with cold water, and set aside. Cook the eggs in simmering water for 9 minutes. Cool in cold water, peel, and quarter.
Melt the butter in a wide saucepan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Add the curry powder, turmeric, and bay leaves. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add the cooked rice and stir to combine with the spiced butter. Add the cream if using. Remove from the heat. Fold through the smoked salmon and spring onions. Squeeze over the lemon juice. Taste for seasoning. Arrange the egg quarters over the top. Scatter with parsley. Serve immediately.
